# `Q-5-19` — Unknown project profile

> An active profile matches no `_quarto-<name>.yml`, no
> `_environment-<name>`, and nothing declared under `profile:`.

## What this means

A profile named `staging` can affect a project in three ways:

- a `_quarto-staging.yml` overlay, merged over `_quarto.yml`
- an `_environment-staging` file, contributing environment variables
- a declaration under `profile:` in `_quarto.yml`

The profile you activated matches none of them, so activating it
changes nothing. Almost always this means the name is misspelled — you
asked for a configuration that does not exist, and got the default one
without noticing.

The render continues with whatever configuration was in effect.

## Why this happens

- **A typo** in `--profile`, in `QUARTO_PROFILE`, or in
  `profile.default`.
- **The overlay file is misnamed.** It must be exactly
  `_quarto-<name>.yml` — `_quarto.staging.yml` and `quarto-staging.yml`
  do not match.
- **The overlay is in the wrong directory.** It belongs next to
  `_quarto.yml` at the project root.
- **A profile used only for conditional content.** If `staging` exists
  purely so `when-profile="staging"` can key off it, there is no
  overlay file to find — see the fix below.

## How to fix

If you meant to select an overlay, check the file name against the
profile name:

```
_quarto.yml
_quarto-staging.yml     ← selected by --profile staging
```

If the profile exists only for conditional content, declare it so
Quarto knows it is real:

```yaml
profile:
  group:
    - [production, staging]
```

or, if it is the profile you want active by default:

```yaml
profile:
  default: staging
```

With the declaration in place, `when-profile="staging"` works and the
warning stops.
